notes.decision: Translated as 'raised up' per terminology rule on ⲧⲟⲩⲱ (preserves vertical/exposing semantics). In context of weeping, likely means 'raised up (their cry/voice) three times.'
Parsed as ⲛⲁⲩ 'see' + 3pl object suffix -ⲍⲟⲩ (Lyc. variant of ⲁⲣⲁⲩ). The construction ⲥⲉⲧⲙ̄ⲛⲁⲩⲍⲟⲩ ⲁⲣⲓⲙⲉ = 'they shall not see them weeping (again)'.

ⲉϩⲁϣⲉ qualitative 'hung, extended'; ⲁⲡⲁⲟⲉ tentatively read as a directional/spatial phrase 'at a distance' or 'far' (possibly from ⲟⲩⲉ 'be far'); ⲟⲩⲃⲏⲩ 'against them.' Translated 'hanging extended at a distance against them' to capture the cosmic looming of Darkness.
ⲛⲉⲍⲥⲉ = Lyc. ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'wake up, rise up.' The future relative 'what shall rise up against them' captures the awakening of dark opposition.
Likely from a verb of hastening/rushing (possibly Lyc. for ϫⲱϣ or ϩⲱϣ 'be in haste') with reflexive 3pl. With ⲁⲍⲟⲩⲛ ⲁⲣⲁϩ 'in unto him' = 'they hastened in unto him.'

Translated 'the chosen [moment]' — using glossary's 'chosen one' (qualitative of ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄) adjectivally to modify an implied moment/time, given the relative clause 'in which the Andrias shall go up.' The doubled -ⲧⲧ suggests the qualitative form. Cf. parallel l.9 omitting ⲡⲥⲁⲧⲧ and using only the demonstrative.

Read as ⲛϭⲓ (subject-marker), introducing 'the souls' as the entity to whom the necessity applies: 'by a necessity, namely the souls who are prepared for Error.' Lycopolitan ⲭ for ϫ regularly attested.

'In the manner that they desired toward it' — the souls' eschatological binding with Darkness mirrors their inner desire for it. Direct correspondence: their eternal state IS the desire they cultivated. ⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓ = Greek ἐπιθυμέω.

'The fourth weeping' — the firmaments themselves constitute this fourth weeping, distinct from three preceding weepings. The ⲡⲱⲩ ⲉⲛ ⲡⲉ phrase clarifies: this fourth weeping is not for their own sake but for the lost souls.

Tentative 'with lamentation' — ⲁⲱⲧ̄ likely Lycopolitan reflex of a verb of lament/groaning (cf. ⲁϣⲁϩⲟⲙ 'sigh, lament'). Etymology uncertain; context (firmaments grieving over souls) supports lament-noun.

Read as a concessive/contrastive perfect-cleft setting up the contrast: although the apostles labored mightily ('gave themselves to every toil'), nevertheless the souls fell into the last error. The cause of the souls' last error is thus their own choice, not any failure of the apostles.

ⲯⲓⲥ rendered 'affliction' — apparent shortened form of θλῖψις (cf. l.3 full form ⲫⲗⲓⲯⲓⲥ). Could be scribal abbreviation. Context (paired with 'taking suffering and crucifixion') strongly supports 'affliction.'

'Desired to take his recompense' — ⲟⲩⲱⲱⲉ = Lyc reflex of ⲟⲩⲱϣⲉ 'wish, desire'; ⲁⲭⲓ = ⲁ-ϫⲓ 'to take/receive.' The apostles refused worldly reward, choosing suffering instead, that the souls might be saved.

Untranslated as the start; this is the continuation of a word from the previous page (no lacuna marker on this page). The visible '...ⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ' may be the end of a compound such as ⲡⲣⲙⲛⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'the New Man' (in glossary) or ⲡⲧⲁⲓⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲃⲣ̄ⲡⲉ 'the New Aeon' (in glossary). The closing line 4 'before God and the apostles' suggests the ending of a doxological/ethical conclusion to the previous kephalaion.
